thread:
mike.dev: quick q — i'm testing the embeddings endpoint with mixed dims (512 + 768) in one request. console shows 'split_count=2' but billing/quotas in the UI still looks weird. whats the canonical routing/quotas semantics here?
anya: short answer: we split the request into homogeneous batches before routing. if you send mixed dims we create 2 jobs.
raj: adding detail — routing picks the minimal number of splits that produce uniform dim shards. we prefer fewer splits even if that means sending an extra small batch vs many tiny ones.
emily: is that behavior documented anywhere? the console UX currently shows only "requests" and an opaque "split_count" metric. product wants to show estimated units and quota impact before you send.
mike.dev: right — customer hit 413s unexpectedly and assumed quota was per-request not per-shard. need clearer preflight and console messaging.
anya: agree. we should emit a preflight header and telemetry event that explains planned splits. e.g. 
```
X-Embed-Preflight: split_plan=2; dims=512,768; est_units=1536
```
so SDKs/console can display it.
raj: +1. impl notes: preflight should run the same logic as router but be cheap (no batching placement). it returns a canonical "split_plan" and estimated token units. fallback: if preflight not supported, router does it on the fly.
sre-jen: watch out for race with quotas. if preflight says "est_units=1536" but peak allocator changes, we still might reject on actual allocate. telemetry needs both preflight_est and final_alloc.
console-bot: preflight.telemetry.event emitted: {"preflight_est":1536, "split_plan":2, "dims":[512,768]}
emily: perf/UX ask: show a small badge before request: "will be split into 2 batches — estimated cost: $0.003" and a link to details. also show a tooltip for "why split?" with a one-line explanation: "mixed-dimension inputs must be served by homogeneous pipelines".
mike.dev: what about soft-quotas / early-failure? policy is currently soft-fail under tenant quota, right? return 429 with body explaining suggested smaller batch.
raj: we have two moving parts: per-shard quota accounting (counts against tenant quota per split) and an early-fastfail threshold that tries to return 413/429 preemptively. proposal: if preflight_est > tenant_quota_remaining then return 429 with 'preflight_quota' hint.
anya: telemetry names proposal: `embed.preflight_est`, `embed.split_plan`, `embed.quota_hit(preflight|final)`. these should be tagged with `route` and `model_variant`.
emily: for console, also send an example payload preview showing how it will be chunked (very short) — helps debugging.
sre-jen: runbook note: if router mismatches preflight due to placement, emit a diagnostic log with request id + preflight_hash + final_hash so we can trace.
mike.dev: rollout plan idea: feature flag `embed_preflight_v2` behind opt-in. A/B in prod for 2 weeks. console shows preflight only for flagged accounts.
raj: implemented a minimal header we can use immediately: `X-Embed-Preflight-Plan: dims=512:count=12,768:count=8; est_units=1536` — SDKs can parse.
anya: we should also update the API contract doc with exact semantics: "server may split mixed-dim inputs into N homogeneous batches; quota charged per batch; preflight returns estimated charge but not guaranteed". legal/customer needs that wording.
emily: UX checklist for console: 1) preflight badge, 2) est cost, 3) split preview toggle, 4) link to docs.
mike.dev: ok i'll draft the API doc blurb + UI mock and throw into the rollout PR. can someone volunteer to wire telemetry metrics?
raj: i'll add the router emission and header.
anya: i'll write the API text and unit tests for preflight parity.
sre-jen: i'll add the runbook snippet and diagnostic logs.
emily: i'll prototype the badge and tooltip in the console sandbox.
mike.dev: perfect. follow-ups: can we decide metric names and a sample preflight response shape today?
anya: sample preflight json (for docs):
```
{
  "split_plan": 2,
  "shards": [{"dim":512,"count":12},{"dim":768,"count":8}],
  "est_units": 1536,
  "quota_ok": false,
  "quota_remaining": 1000
}
```
mike.dev: nice. emily — feels good to show that in the console as a compact row.
emily: yep. i'll mock it. thanks all. :thumbsup:
